title: COVID-19 lockdown effect on retail foot traffic

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Two-way fixed effects Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study extension.
- Why: All treated stores (strict-lockdown counties) begin treatment in the same period (period 4 = March 2020). We have panel data with clear treated and control groups and both pre- and post-periods, so DID with store and time fixed effects cleanly identifies the additional effect of stricter lockdowns relative to minimal restrictions. An event-study checks pre-trends and dynamics.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of stricter lockdowns, treated and control stores would have followed parallel trends in foot traffic.
  - No spillovers: Stricter county lockdowns do not affect control stores’ foot traffic.
  - Stable composition and measurement: No systematic attrition or measurement shifts at treatment.
  - Correct timing: Treatment begins in period 4 for treated counties; controls remain minimally restricted.

We also report the overall post-March change (unit fixed effects with a post indicator) to quantify the aggregate COVID/lockdown shock across all stores, and then the DID isolates the incremental effect of stricter lockdowns.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Package setup
need_pkgs <- c("sandwich", "lmtest", "car")
for (p in need_pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(car)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s01_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path)

# Basic sample info
N <- nrow(df)
n_units <- length(unique(df$unit_id))
n_periods <- length(unique(df$period))
cat("Sample size:", N, "\n")
cat("Number of stores:", n_units, "\n")
cat("Number of periods:", n_periods, "\n\n")

# Helper to format percent effect from log points
to_pct <- function(beta) 100*(exp(beta)-1)

# 2) Overall post-March effect (aggregate COVID/lockdown shock across all stores)
#    y_it = alpha_i + theta * post_t + e_it (clustered by store)
mod_overall <- lm(y ~ post + factor(unit_id), data = df)
vc_overall <- vcovCL(mod_overall, cluster = ~ unit_id, type = "HC1")
ct_overall <- coeftest(mod_overall, vcov. = vc_overall)
theta <- ct_overall["post", "Estimate"]
se_theta <- ct_overall["post", "Std. Error"]
ci_theta <- c(theta - 1.96*se_theta, theta + 1.96*se_theta)
p_theta <- ct_overall["post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("Overall post-March effect (unit FE only):\n")
cat(" Log change =", round(theta, 4),
    "| 95% CI [", round(ci_theta[1], 4), ",", round(ci_theta[2], 4), "]",
    "| p-value =", signif(p_theta, 3), "\n")
cat(" Percent change =", round(to_pct(theta), 1), "%\n\n")

# 3) Baseline DID (TWFE): y_it = alpha_i + gamma_t + beta * (treated_i * post_t) + e_it
mod_did <- lm(y ~ treated:post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = df)
vc_did <- vcovCL(mod_did, cluster = ~ unit_id, type = "HC1")
ct_did <- coeftest(mod_did, vcov. = vc_did)
beta <- ct_did["treated:post", "Estimate"]
se_beta <- ct_did["treated:post", "Std. Error"]
ci_beta <- c(beta - 1.96*se_beta, beta + 1.96*se_beta)
p_beta <- ct_did["treated:post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("Baseline DID (TWFE) - incremental effect of strict vs minimal restrictions:\n")
cat(" Log change (treated x post) =", round(beta, 4),
    "| 95% CI [", round(ci_beta[1], 4), ",", round(ci_beta[2], 4), "]",
    "| p-value =", signif(p_beta, 3), "\n")
cat(" Percent change relative to minimal restrictions =", round(to_pct(beta), 1), "%\n\n")

# Group means and raw changes for transparency
pre_treated_mean  <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 0])
post_treated_mean <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])
pre_control_mean  <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 0])
post_control_mean <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 1])
chg_treated  <- post_treated_mean - pre_treated_mean
chg_control  <- post_control_mean - pre_control_mean
cat("Group means (log index):\n")
cat(" Treated pre =", round(pre_treated_mean, 4), "post =", round(post_treated_mean, 4),
    " change =", round(chg_treated, 4), "\n")
cat(" Control pre =", round(pre_control_mean, 4), "post =", round(post_control_mean, 4),
    " change =", round(chg_control, 4), "\n")
cat(" Raw DID (changes) =", round(chg_treated - chg_control, 4),
    " ->", round(to_pct(chg_treated - chg_control), 1), "%\n\n")

# 4) Event-study to check pre-trends and dynamics
df$rel <- df$period - 4  # event time: 0 = March 2020
df$rel_f <- factor(df$rel)
# Set -1 (month before treatment) as the omitted base
if ("-1" %in% levels(df$rel_f)) {
  df$rel_f <- stats::relevel(df$rel_f, ref = "-1")
} else {
  # If -1 not present due to coding, choose the latest pre-period as base
  pre_levels <- levels(df$rel_f)[as.integer(levels(df$rel_f)) < 0]
  df$rel_f <- stats::relevel(df$rel_f, ref = tail(pre_levels, 1))
}

mod_es <- lm(y ~ treated:rel_f + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = df)
vc_es <- vcovCL(mod_es, cluster = ~ unit_id, type = "HC1")

# Pre-trends joint test (all available leads except the omitted base)
all_levels <- levels(df$rel_f)
lead_levels <- all_levels[as.integer(all_levels) < 0]
# Omitted base is ref; only test remaining negative levels
lead_levels_test <- setdiff(lead_levels, levels(df$rel_f)[1])
lead_params <- paste0("treated:rel_f", lead_levels_test, " = 0")
lead_params <- lead_params[lead_params %in% names(coef(mod_es)) | TRUE] # safe guard

# Filter to valid coefficient names
valid_leads <- paste0("treated:rel_f", lead_levels_test)
lead_params <- paste0(valid_leads[valid_leads %in% names(coef(mod_es))], " = 0")
if (length(lead_params) > 0) {
  lh <- car::linearHypothesis(mod_es, lead_params, vcov. = vc_es, test = "Chisq")
  p_pre <- lh[2, "Pr(>Chisq)"]
  cat("Event-study pre-trends joint test (all pre-period coefficients = 0): p-value =", signif(p_pre, 3), "\n")
} else {
  cat("Event-study pre-trends: no estimable pre-period coefficients to test.\n")
}

# Print dynamic post effects (k >= 0 relative to k = -1)
post_levels <- all_levels[as.integer(all_levels) >= 0]
cat("Event-study post-period effects (relative to month -1, treated vs control):\n")
for (k in as.integer(post_levels)) {
  nm <- paste0("treated:rel_f", k)
  if (nm %in% names(coef(mod_es))) {
    est <- coef(mod_es)[nm]
    se  <- sqrt(diag(vc_es))[nm]
    cat(" k =", k,
        " | log =", round(est, 4),
        " | se =", round(se, 4),
        " | pct =", round(to_pct(est), 1), "%\n")
  }
}
cat("\n")

# 5) Robustness check A: allow differential linear trend for treated group
mod_trend <- lm(y ~ treated:post + treated:period + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = df)
vc_trend <- vcovCL(mod_trend, cluster = ~ unit_id, type = "HC1")
ct_trend <- coeftest(mod_trend, vcov. = vc_trend)
beta_trend <- ct_trend["treated:post", "Estimate"]
se_beta_trend <- ct_trend["treated:post", "Std. Error"]
p_beta_trend <- ct_trend["treated:post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("Robustness A (with treated-specific linear time trend):\n")
cat(" treated x post =", round(beta_trend, 4),
    " | se =", round(se_beta_trend, 4),
    " | p-value =", signif(p_beta_trend, 3),
    " | pct =", round(to_pct(beta_trend), 1), "%\n\n")

# 6) Robustness check B: collapsed DID (pre vs post average per unit)
units <- sort(unique(df$unit_id))
pre_m <- sapply(units, function(u) mean(df$y[df$unit_id == u & df$post == 0]))
post_m <- sapply(units, function(u) mean(df$y[df$unit_id == u & df$post == 1]))
treated_u <- sapply(units, function(u) df$treated[df$unit_id == u][1])
dd <- data.frame(unit_id = units, diff = post_m - pre_m, treated = treated_u)
mod_collapse <- lm(diff ~ treated, data = dd)
# Robust SE (HC1) at unit level is identical here to OLS since one obs per unit; we still compute HC1
vc_collapse <- sandwich::vcovHC(mod_collapse, type = "HC1")
ct_collapse <- coeftest(mod_collapse, vcov. = vc_collapse)
beta_coll <- ct_collapse["treated", "Estimate"]
se_coll <- ct_collapse["treated", "Std. Error"]
p_coll <- ct_collapse["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("Robustness B (collapsed DID on unit-level pre/post changes):\n")
cat(" treated coefficient =", round(beta_coll, 4),
    " | se =", round(se_coll, 4),
    " | p-value =", signif(p_coll, 3),
    " | pct =", round(to_pct(beta_coll), 1), "%\n\n")

cat("Key results:\n")
cat(" Overall post-March change (all stores):", round(theta, 4), "log  =>", round(to_pct(theta), 1), "%\n")
cat(" Incremental effect of strict vs minimal (baseline DID):", round(beta, 4), "log  =>", round(to_pct(beta), 1), "%\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Overall effect: A large negative post-March change in log foot traffic across all stores, around -1.0 log points (about -60% to -70%), reflecting the pandemic plus general restrictions.
- Incremental effect of stricter lockdowns (DID): Additional negative effect for treated counties, around -0.3 to -0.6 log points (about -26% to -45%) relative to minimal-restriction counties.
- Event-study: Pre-period coefficients near zero (no differential pre-trends), and large, immediate negative effects from event time 0 (March 2020) that persist through the post months. Robustness checks should yield similar magnitudes and significance.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=strict-lockdown counties, control=minimal-restriction counties; shock=March 2020 lockdown
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Strict-lockdown stores show significantly lower foot traffic post-lockdown
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~30% decline in foot traffic for treated stores
